title: Coupled-channel approach to scattering of hybrid excitons
authors: Yasufumi Nakano, Meera M. Parish, Jesper Levinsen
abstract: We consider the interactions of hybrid excitons in a two-dimensional semiconductor bilayer, where spatially direct and indirect excitons are hybridized by interlayer charge-carrier tunneling. Starting from a microscopic electron-hole description, we construct realistic pseudopotentials for exciton-exciton interactions and use them as inputs to a coupled-channel scattering integral equation. This enables non-perturbative calculations of hybrid-exciton scattering beyond standard perturbative theories, and highlights the importance of energy-dependent scattering and channel mixing. In particular, we show that the interaction strength of hybrid excitons exhibits a rapid growth with increasing energy, which we find is inherited from their indirect-exciton component. We further demonstrate that dielectric screening affects the direct and indirect channels in distinct ways, leading to markedly different interaction strengths across experimentally relevant dielectric environments. Finally, we show that the hybrid-exciton scattering strength can be electrically tuned via the Stark shift, which controls the direct-indirect detuning and hence the hybridization of the two exciton modes.
summary: This paper develops a non-perturbative coupled-channel theory to calculate the scattering of hybrid excitons in 2D semiconductor bilayers. By incorporating interlayer tunneling and using a T-matrix approach, the authors demonstrate that exciton interactions are strongly dependent on energy and can be precisely controlled by an external electric field via the Stark shift. This offers a powerful theoretical framework for designing quantum optical devices based on tunable exciton interactions.
main_problem: To perform non-perturbative calculations of hybrid exciton scattering beyond standard perturbative theories.
main_result: The study shows that the hybrid-exciton scattering strength can be electrically tuned via the Stark shift, and its interaction properties are governed by a coupled-channel T-matrix approach.
method: The authors construct realistic pseudopotentials from microscopic descriptions and employ a non-perturbative coupled-channel scattering integral equation (T-matrix approach).
model_or_system: The system is hybrid excitons formed in a two-dimensional semiconductor bilayer, involving the hybridization of spatially direct (DX) and indirect (IX) exciton states via interlayer tunneling.
key_observables: Hybrid-exciton T matrices, interaction strength dependence on Stark shift ($\Delta$), and exciton weights (DX/IX fractions).
important_parameters: Dielectric constant ($\kappa$), electric field induced detuning ($\Delta$), and momentum transfer ($q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes equal masses for electrons and holes, and uses a projection method onto the two-exciton subspace.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic hybridization in $	ext{MoS}_2$ bilayers, energy levels vs. dielectric constant, and T-matrices showing dependence on the Stark shift.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the microscopic Hamiltonian to constructing pseudopotentials, applying a coupled-channel T-matrix formalism for non-perturbative scattering, and finally analyzing tuning mechanisms via the Stark effect.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools (coupled-channel T-matrix) to model interacting excitons in low-dimensional materials, which is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated light-matter interactions in quantum optics and condensed matter physics.
